newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil civil service reform vote verified in count.
newsitem.headline: Brazil civil service reform vote verified in count.

text.p: Officials confirmed that Brazil's lower house Wednesday approved by 309 votes, one more than the minimum needed, a bill reforming civil service.

The officials said deputies would vote next week an amendment setting a higher salary ceiling for elected officials and some other public servants, a motion that faces considerable controversy on the floor of the house.
The original vote count showed 308 votes in favor of the bill, a number which was revised during the manual recount of the electronic vote.
"We approved the bill, which was the important objective. The (extra salary ceiling) will only be voted next week," said Benito Gama, the government's chief whip.
The bill approved by the Chamber of Deputies sets a cap on public sector salaries of 10,800 reais per month.

In an agreement struck with a block of deputies earning more than that, the government agreed to allow elected officials and some other civil servants to earn a pension on top of their salary of up to another 10,800 reais a month. The additional pension is known as the extra salary ceiling.
Gama said the government grudgingly supported the extra salary ceiling and expected it to be approved next week.
The civil service reform bill must still pass through another lower house vote before going twice through the Senate, each time needing a three-fifths majority.
